The information regarding the accident was first received vide DD No. 3A at about 12:02 midnight, upon which police officials immediately reached the spot.
Both vehicles were found at the spot in a damaged condition.
The accident was witnessed by injured persons, nearby public persons and police officials, and all injured persons were promptly removed to hospitals.
As per the DAR and the statements of police officials, Hari Om was rescued from the driver's seat of the XUV vehicle, whereas Kuldeep was rescued from the co-driver seat.
This position is consistently reflected in the contemporaneous police records and statements.
The medical records from AIIMS Trauma Centre and Apollo Hospital further corroborate the occurrence of the accident as well as the rescue operations.

(h) It is also to be noted that the identity of the driver of the offending vehicle has already been conclusively examined and adjudicated upon in the connected cross cases relating to the same accident.

Based upon the DAR, site plan, charge-sheet, testimonies of victims, and other material on record, it has already been held that Hari Om was driving the offending XUV at the relevant time,
whereas Kuldeep was sitting alongside him.

The said findings have attained finality for the purpose of appreciation of evidence in the present claim and cannot be permitted to be unsettled merely on the basis of a self-serving statement of Kuldeep.
(I) There is a clear inconsistency regarding who was actually driving the XUV vehicle.

Although Kuldeep claims that he himself was driving the vehicle, he admittedly never informed MACT No.
231/2019 Kuldeep Vs. Sachin & Ors. Page No. 16 of 20 (rpt) the police of this fact at any stage, nor did he question the investigation or file any protest petition before the learned Magistrate.

sentences.text: (j) It is evident from the record that the version now put forth by Kuldeep is in clear contradiction to the police investigation, charge-sheet and consistent testimonies of other injured/victims.

No plausible explanation has been offered as to why, if Kuldeep was actually driving the vehicle, the charge-sheet was filed against Hari Om alone, nor why Kuldeep did not take any legal recourse to challenge the investigation.

(k) Significantly, no protest petition was filed before the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, no complaint was made to any superior police authority, and no independent material was brought on record to dislodge the findings of the investigating agency.

The conduct of Kuldeep, therefore,
clearly indicates an afterthought aimed at shifting the role of driver, which is impermissible in law.
(l) Equally important is the fact that no allegation whatsoever has been levelled against Sachin, the driver of the victim vehicle.

There is no FIR, no charge-sheet, no complaint, and no material on Kuldeep vs Sachin Kumar on 20 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40444134/
10 record suggesting even remotely that the accident occurred due to any rashness or negligence on his part.
The investigating agency did not find any fault with the manner in which the victim vehicle was being driven, and no contrary evidence has been produced before this Tribunal.
Thus, the plea of negligence of the victim vehicle is wholly unsubstantiated and deserves outright rejection.

(m) On the contrary, the DAR, site plan and mechanical MACT No. 231/2019 Kuldeep Vs. Sachin &
Ors. Page No. 17 of 20 (rpt) inspection report consistently show that the XUV vehicle was found on the wrong side of the road.
Even though the road at the place of accident did not have a physical divider, it was meant for two-way traffic, and entering the opposite lane constitutes a clear violation of traffic norms.
This circumstance does not support the version of the claimant fastening negligence upon the Celerio vehicle.
There is also no evidence on record to establish that the Celerio was being driven at an excessive speed or in a negligent manner.

(o) The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, though a welfare forum, proceeds on the principles of equity and good conscience.

The claimant is required to establish negligence and must approach the Tribunal with fairness, consistency and bona fide conduct.
In the present case, the claimant's version regarding the manner of accident and the identity of the driver of the XUV remains uncertain and inconsistent with the contemporaneous record.
The claimant has also failed to discharge the foundational burden of proving rash or negligent driving on the part of the Celerio vehicle.
These deficiencies go to the root of the matter.
